 Judgment

This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking
compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.
2. The case of the pet

itioner is as follows:-
That on 31-12-2024 at about 9-00 to 9.30 a.m., petitioner was proceeding in the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-07-X-6045 as a pillion rider and one Ranjith Kumar was riding the said motorcycle from Kolar to Bengaluru road and when they reached in front of Coffee Day, Kolar, at that time, the driver of JCB bearing Reg.No.KA-07-N-2896 which was proceeding ahead of the petitioner's vehicle in a rash and negligent manner, suddenly took the vehicle towards right side without giving any signal and dashed to the motor cycle, result of which the petitioner and rider fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to SNR Hospital, Kolar and then shifted to Sanskriti Hospital wherein admitted as an inpatient.
So far, the petitioner has spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.
3. Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy.
He was aged about 21 years.
He was working as labourer and earning more than sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability, loss of future income and other pecuniary and non- pecuniary damages.
4. Respondent no.1/
the RC owner of JCB bearing Reg.No.KA-07-N-2896 has remained absent.
Hence he was placed ex-parte.

5. The Respondent no.2/the insurer of JCB bearing Reg.No.KA-07-N-2896 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent no.2 has contended that the insured vehicle was not involved in the accident, that the petitioner in collusion with the jurisdictional police and the owner of the vehicle has fixed the vehicle for unlawful gain.

It is further contended that the driver of insured vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license and that the rider of motor cycle being a tort feasor is not entitled to claim compensation.
6.
Heard the arguments and perused the entire materials placed on record.

7. Based on the pleadings, this tribunal framed the following:
Hitesh B vs Narayana Swamy T on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51233764/
2 ISSUES 1.

sentences.text:
Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained injuries on account of road traffic accident on 31.12.2024 at about 9-00 to 9.30 am., in front of infront of Coffee Day, Kolar to Bengaluru Road, NH-75, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of RC owner of JCB bearing Reg.No.KA-07-N-2896?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3. What order or Award ?
8.
The petitioner got examined himself as Pw1 and two witnesses are examined as PW.2 and PW.3 and got marked documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P18.
On the other, the respondent no.2 has not adduced any evidence on its behalf.

9. My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following;

REASONS 10. Issue No.1:- In order to explain the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle,
P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 31-12-2024 at about 9-00 to 9.30 a.m., when the petitioner was proceeding in the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-07-X-6045 as a pillion rider and one Ranjith Kumar was riding the said motorcycle from Kolar to Bengaluru road and when they reached in front of Coffee Day, Kolar, at that time, the driver of JCB bearing Reg.No.KA-07-N-2896 (hereinafter referred as the offending vehicle) which was proceeding ahead of the petitioner's vehicle in a rash and negligent manner,
suddenly took the vehicle towards right side without giving any signal and dashed to the motor cycle, result of which the petitioner and rider fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
11.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 6 which are the police records such as F.I.R with complaint, Spot mahazar, IMV report,
wound certificate, charge sheet, statement of petitioner, etc.,
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Ranjith Kumar R case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.3/2025 by Vemgal Police Station for the offence punishable under section 125(a), 281 of BNS.

After completion of investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under section Hitesh B vs Narayana Swamy T on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51233764/
3 125(a), 281, 125(b) of BNS.
13.

entities.text: Hitesh B vs Narayana Swamy T
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned counsel for respondent no.2 has much argued about the delay in lodging the complaint and submitted that the offending vehicle was falsely implicated in the accident.
14. If the police records are perused, it is true that accident in question has occurred on 31-12-2024 about 9-00 am., and complaint came to be lodged on 03-01-2025 at about 12-45 pm.,
There is delay of three days in lodging the complaint.
As per the complaint both the petitioner and rider of the motorcycle had sustained injuries and both of them were taking treatment at SNR Hospital, Kolar.
It is the rider of the motorcycle by name Ranjith has lodged the complaint after his discharge from the hospital.

Further if the MLC extract as per Ex.P16 issued from SNR District Hospital, Kolar is perused, on the date of accident itself the petitioner had taken treatment in the said hospital on the alleged history of RTA between two wheeler and JCB on 31-12-2024 at around 9.15 am., near Narasapura Bridge, Narasapura.
Hence, it can be said that though there was delay in lodging the complaint but petitioner has taken treatment on the alleged history of RTA hit by JCB on the date of accident itself.
Hence, the delay in lodging the complaint has been satisfactorily explained.

15. So far as the dispute raised as to the involvement of offending vehicle, is concerned, the owner/driver of the offending vehicle have not contested the petition and they have not denied the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
Admittedly after investigation, charge sheet was filed against the driver of the offending vehicle.
The driver/owner of the offending vehicle have not challenged the charge sheet.
The respondents have not placed any iota of evidence to prove that offending vehicle was not involved in the accident.

16. So far as the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is concerned, as per the police records and as per the evidence of PW.1, at the time of accident petitioner as pillion rider was proceeding from Kolar towards Bengaluru.
The offending vehicle was proceeding on the same direction in front of the motorcycle.

As per the evidence of PW.1 and as borne out by police records,
the driver of the offending vehicle by driving the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner suddenly took the vehicle towards the right side of the road and the rider of the motorcycle who was proceeding behind the offending vehicle without anticipating the offending vehicle taking sudden right turn, came in contact with the offending vehicle.
When the driver of the offending vehicle was taking the vehicle towards right side he has to put indicator or manual sign.
But without giving any such sign or signal, the driver of the offending vehicle in careless manner taken the vehicle towards the right side.
Hence, it can be said that the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is the sole cause for the accident.
Hence, issue no.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
17. Issue No.2:-
The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., Wound certificate and discharge summaries which are marked at Ex.P4, Ex.P7 and Ex.P12.
On going through the medical documents it reveal that petitioner has taken treatment at SNR District Hospital, Kolar from 31-12-2024 to 05-01-2025.
Thereafter the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient at Sanskriti Hospital for two times ie., from 18-01-2025 to 20-01-2025 and 25.01.2025 to 27.01.2025.
The petitioner has taken treatment in all for a period of 11 days.

As per the wound certificate, petitioner has sustained Hitesh B vs Narayana Swamy T on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51233764/
4

entities.text: Hitesh B vs Narayana Swamy T
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: three injuries which are grievous in nature.
18. Dr.Nagaraj.
B.N - Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho & Dental Center is examined as PW.2 and through him clinical note and x-rays are marked as Ex.P13 and Ex.P14.

PW.3 has deposed that he examined the petitioner on 17-12-2025 clinically, radiologically for assessment of disability and that petitioner has sustained permanent disability of left lower limb at 40% and on whole body at 13%.
19.
If the cross examination of PW.2 is perused, he has not given treatment to the petitioner at any point of time.

It is admitted by PW.2 that what ever the physical disability allegedly suffered by the petitioner one stated in his affidavit are not stated in the wound certificate and also in any of the medical records.

Admittedly petitioner has taken conservative treatment and as per the evidence of PW.2 all the injuries are healed and the percentage of disability allegedly suffered by the petitioner does not come in the way of his future earning capacity.

20. Though the PW.2 has assessed the disability at 13% on whole body but when as per the evidence of PW.2, said percentage of disability does not come in the way of the earning capacity of petitioner and when petitioner has taken only conservative treatment and all the injuries are healed, there is no reason to say that the alleged percentage of disability would come in the way of discharging the duties by the petitioner.
In (2011) 1 SCC 343 Raj Kumar V/s Ajay Kumar and another.

entities.text: (2011) 1 SCC 343 Raj Kumar V/s Ajay Kumar and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case detailed principle was laid down for assessment of loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
It was held that "In a disability certificate extent of disability of a limb (or part of the body) cannot be assumed to be extent of disability of whole body.
The Tribunal should not mechanically apply percentage of permanent physical disability as percentage of economic loss or loss of earning capacity but must assess functional disability.

It was further observed that where the claimant suffers a permanent disability as a result of injuries, the assessment of compensation under the head loss of future earnings would depend upon the effect and impact of such permanent disability on his earning capacity".
21.
Hence, this court declines to consider the disability of petitioner one assessed by the PW.2 and decline to award compensation under the head loss of future income due to the disability .
Since petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and has taken treatment for 11 days, it would have caused some amount of loss of amenities and discomfort.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort but not under the head loss of future income due to disability.
22. Hence, considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment, this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
23. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained three grievous injuries and five simple injuries.

Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained, time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment, it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.80,000/- towards pain and suffering.

5 24.

sentences.text: So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is concerned, he has produced 7 medical bills for Rs.1,11,872/- as per Ex.P8 and 2 cash receipts at Ex.P9.

Hence, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head medical expenses to the tune of Rs.1,11,872/-.
25.
It is stated that petitioner was doing Labourer work and earning sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
But to substantiate the said contention petitioner has not produced any materials.

Hence this court considering the age of petitioner, year of accident and the place of residence, considers the income of the petitioner as Rs.16,500/- p.m.
26.
The petitioner has sustained three grievous injury and has taken treatment for 11 days as inpatient in SNR Hospita, Kolar and Sanskriti Hospital, Bangalore.
Hence the nature of injury sustained by the petitioner which is grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of 3 months as complete laid down period.

Hence taking in to consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation this court takes the loss of income during the laid down period as Rs.16,500/- p.m., for 3 months.
Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.49,500/- (16,500X3) towards loss of income during the laid down period .
27. From the evidence of PW.1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment at SNR Hospita, Kolar and Sanskriti Hospital, Bangalore.
Further for 11 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment.
He has taken nourishment and needs further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.

Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.35,000/- taking into consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2024.
28.
The petitioner has contended that, he was aged about 20 years as on the date of accident.
Petitioner has produced Ex.P10/Aadhar card of the petitioner which shows his date of birth as 08-01-2004.
That means petitioner was aged about 20 years.
Hence this court has taken the age of the petitioner as 20 years at the time of accident.
29. The petitioner at his age of 20 years has suffered disability, hence definitely some amount of discomfort and loss of amenities would have caused to the petitioner.
Hence he is entitled for sum of Rs.2,75,000/- towards loss of amenities and discomfort.

Thus the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
 Sl. Heads Amount  No.
1. Towards pain & sufferings Rs. 80,000/-

2 . Medical expenses Rs. 1,11,872/-
3. Towards loss of income during Rs. 49,500/-
 laid up period 4.

Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 35,000/-
 charges and nourishing food 5. Loss of comfort and amenities Rs. 2,75,000/-

Total Rs. 5,51,372/-

sentences.text: Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.5,51,372/- (Rupees Five Lakh Fifty One Thousand Three Hundred Seventy Two only).
30. As regarding liability is concerned, respondent no.1 is the RC owner and respondent no.2 is the Insurer of the offending vehicle.
There is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of the offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no.2 this court directs the respondent no.2 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered.
31. Issue No.3:
In the light of the findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this Issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.5,51,372/- (Rupees Five Lakh Fifty One Thousand Three Hundred Seventy Two only) with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit. .
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the said amount and interest, 40% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

On deposit of the said amount and interest, 40% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
